hints: Focus on the structure of propyne first, it is unsymmetrical so where H and Br add really matters.
Remember Markovnikov's rule: H adds to the carbon that already has more H atoms, while Br adds to the more substituted carbon.
Apply that rule twice in a row, since excess HBr means two additions, and see which carbon ends up collecting both Br atoms.
walkthrough:
**Draw out propyne clearly**

Start by writing propyne as $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$. Notice the triple bond is between C2 (joined to $\text{CH}_3$, with no H) and C1 (with one H). This difference is the key to Markovnikov orientation.

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{H}$$

**First addition of HBr gives a bromoalkene**

Add one $\text{H-Br}$ across the triple bond. By Markovnikov, H goes to the carbon with more H (the $\text{CH}$ end) and Br goes to the more substituted carbon (the $\text{C-CH}_3$ end).

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}=\text{CH}_2$$
This is 2-bromopropene, the main intermediate.

**Second addition of HBr gives a dibromoalkane**

Now add a second $\text{H-Br}$ across the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ of $\text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}=\text{CH}_2$. Again H adds to the carbon with more H (the $\text{CH}_2$ end) and Br adds to the more substituted carbon (the one already bearing Br and $\text{CH}_3$).

$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{CBr}_2-\text{CH}_3$$
Both Br atoms end up on the same middle carbon, giving 2,2-dibromopropane.

options.A: This is 1,3-dibromopropane, with Br atoms on opposite ends. This would require anti-Markovnikov addition at both stages, putting Br on the less substituted carbons each time, which is the opposite of the rule.
options.B: This is 1,1-dibromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHBr}_2$. This puts both Br atoms on the terminal carbon. That would mean Br added to the carbon that already had most H in the first step, which violates Markovnikov's rule.
options.C: This is 1,2-dibromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_2\text{Br}$, with one Br on each carbon of the original multiple bond. This happens if one addition follows Markovnikov and the other does not. With excess HBr and Markovnikov control at each stage, both Br atoms go to the same carbon.
options.D: This is 2,2-dibromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CBr}_2\text{CH}_3$. Both additions place Br on the more substituted middle carbon (C2) and H on the terminal carbon, exactly as Markovnikov's rule predicts for two stages. Lovely, consistent double Markovnikov addition.
